title: AXIOMA: keeping science-card combo scoring legible without slowing play
author: Typical-Instance-376
selftext: I'm Samuel, a teacher and creator of AXIOMA, a science-themed card game built around math, physics and chemistry. AI tools are part of my development workflow; the design question I'm working on is how to show why a combination scored without stopping every turn to explain the rules. I'm trying to keep the score breakdown readable during play. For people building games with AI-assisted workflows: what UI patterns help explain combos while keeping pace? Short gameplay: [https://youtu.be/jVwt6M4J1GA](https://youtu.be/jVwt6M4J1GA)

comments.author: Typical-Instance-376
comments.body:
Update: AXIOMA is now available on Steam, with English supported: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5308770/AXIOMA/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5308770/AXIOMA/)



The store page discloses AI-generated artwork, text and translations, with no live AI generation. That makes the wording of science cards worth discussing alongside the combo UI: what checks do you use to keep translated card text clear without changing the scientific meaning or the rule?



Here is a 19-second real gameplay clip. The interface in this clip is Portuguese, not English: [https://www.tiktok.com/@samuel.isidoro.qu/video/7697295461660577076](https://www.tiktok.com/@samuel.isidoro.qu/video/7697295461660577076)
